To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a facile synthetic method for the synthesis of one-dimensional nanostructured thermoelectric materials and have demonstrated the potential of these materials for thermoelectric applications.

the thermoelectric properties (i.e., Seebeck coefficient and electrical and thermal conductivity) of one‐dimensionally segmented and core/shell heterojunctions and hollow nanostructures can be optimized to enhance thermoelectric performance.

we have successfully synthesized Bi2Te3 hollow nanotubes and Te/Bi core–shell nanowires, and we have demonstrated that the thermoelectric properties can be optimized by tuning the shell thickness and the diameter of the hollow nanostructures, and that the thermoelectrics performance of these nanostructured materials is significantly enhanced as compared to the bulk materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of novel nanostructures for thermoelectric applications, the study of their thermoelectric properties, and the development of a theoretical model to describe the thermoelectric transport properties of these materials.
the development of novel nanostructured materials for thermoelectric applications.
the development of novel nanomaterials and their application in the field of thermoelectric energy conversion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nanostructures have been proven to be a viable approach to improving the thermoelectric performance of materials.
the thermoelectric properties are strongly affected by the synthesis method and growth mechanism of nanostructures.
nanostructures have the potential for thermoelectric applications and further studies are necessary for their development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermoelectric properties can be optimized by controlling the composition, structure, and dimension of nanostructures.
nanostructured materials have great potential for improving the thermoelectric performance of materials.
the thermoelectric property of nanostructures is strongly related to the structure and morphology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermoelectric performance of nanostructures can be improved by controlling their size, shape, and composition.
the thermoelectric properties can be improved by optimizing the structural parameters, including the diameter, length, and composition of the nanowire and nanotube.

the thermoelectric properties can be improved by controlling the growth mechanism and the composition of the heterostructures and nanotubes, and the thermoelectric figure of merit can reach 0.8 at 300 K.
